questions.stem:
The major product $P$ of the following reaction is:
$$\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv C-CH_3 \xrightarrow{Na / liq. NH_3} P}$$
questions.solution: The reduction of an internal alkyne (like but-2-yne) with sodium in liquid ammonia (Birch reduction) selectively yields a trans-alkene. Thus, the major product is trans-but-2-ene.

questions.stem:
The major product formed in the following reaction is:
$$\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv C-CH_3} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Na / \text{liquid } NH_3}} \text{Product}$$
questions.solution: The reduction of an internal alkyne with sodium in liquid ammonia (Birch reduction) selectively yields the corresponding \textit{trans}-alkene. Thus, but-2-yne is reduced to \textit{trans}-but-2-ene.

questions.stem:
The major product of the following reaction is:
$$\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{CH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Hg}^{2+}/\mathrm{H}^+} \text{Product}$$
questions.solution: Hydration of propyne ($\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{CH}$) in the presence of dilute $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$ and $\mathrm{HgSO}_4$ (Kucherov's reaction) follows Markovnikov's rule to give an unstable enol intermediate [$\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C(OH)}=\mathrm{CH}_2$] which tautomerizes to acetone (propanone, $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COCH}_3$).

questions.stem: When 1-butyne undergoes hydration in the presence of $\mathrm{Hg^{2+}/H^+}$, the major product formed is a ketone. The number of $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atoms in the major product is _________.
questions.solution:
Hydration of 1-butyne ($\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-C\equiv CH}$) with $\mathrm{Hg^{2+}/H^+}$ gives butanone ($\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CO-CH_3}$).
In butanone:
- Carbon-1 ($\mathrm{-CH_3}$): $sp^3$
- Carbon-2 ($\mathrm{-CO-}$): $sp^2$
- Carbon-3 ($\mathrm{-CH_2-}$): $sp^3$
- Carbon-4 ($\mathrm{-CH_3}$): $sp^3$
Thus, the number of $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atoms is 3.

questions.stem: When propyne is treated with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ in the presence of $\mathrm{Hg^{2+}}$ at $333\ \mathrm{K}$, the major product formed is:
questions.solution: Hydration of propyne ($\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv CH}$) using $\mathrm{dil.\ H_2SO_4 / Hg^{2+}}$ occurs via Markovnikov's addition of water to yield an unstable enol intermediate $\mathrm{CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2}$, which tautomerizes rapidly to give acetone (propanone, $\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_3}$).

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds reacts with $\mathrm{NaNH_2}$ to give a sodium salt?
questions.solution: Terminal alkynes like but-1-yne have acidic acetylenic hydrogens ($\mathrm{sp}$ hybridized carbon) which can react with a strong base like $\mathrm{NaNH_2}$ to form sodium acetylide.

questions.stem: Which of the following hydrocarbons will react with ammoniacal silver nitrate solution to give a white precipitate?
questions.solution: Ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens' reagent) reacts only with terminal alkynes (which possess an acidic acetylenic hydrogen) to form silver acetylides (white precipitate). But-1-yne ($\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{C\equiv CH}$) is a terminal alkyne, whereas But-2-yne is an internal alkyne.

questions.stem: The number of $sp^3$ hybridized carbons present in the major product obtained when 3-methylbut-1-yne undergoes hydration in the presence of $\mathrm{Hg^{2+}/H^+}$ is _________.
questions.solution:
Hydration of 3-methylbut-1-yne ($\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH-C\equiv CH}$) with $\mathrm{Hg^{2+}/H^+}$ gives 3-methylbutan-2-one ($\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH-CO-CH_3}$).
Let us count the hybridization of each carbon in $\mathrm{\overset{5}{C}H_3-\overset{4}{C}H(CH_3)-\overset{2}{C}(=O)-\overset{1}{C}H_3}$:
- $\mathrm{C1}$: $sp^3$
- $\mathrm{C2}$: $sp^2$
- $\mathrm{C3}$ (methyl group on C4): $sp^3$
- $\mathrm{C4}$: $sp^3$
- $\mathrm{C5}$: $sp^3$
Thus, there are 4 $sp^3$ hybridized carbons.

questions.stem: Which of the following alkynes on hydration with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ in the presence of $\mathrm{HgSO_4}$ gives a ketone as the only major product?
questions.solution: Hydration of ethyne ($\mathrm{HC\equiv CH}$) yields acetaldehyde (an aldehyde). Any other terminal alkyne, such as propyne ($\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv CH}$), undergoes Markovnikov addition of water followed by tautomerisation to yield a ketone (acetone).

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will yield a red precipitate of copper acetylide when treated with ammoniacal cuprous chloride?
questions.solution: Ammoniacal cuprous chloride ($\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2 + \text{NH}_4\text{OH}$) reacts specifically with terminal alkynes (which have acidic acetylenic hydrogens) to form a red precipitate of copper acetylide. But-1-yne is a terminal alkyne.

questions.stem: When propyne is treated with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ in the presence of $\mathrm{HgSO_4}$, the major product formed is:
questions.solution:
Hydration of propyne via Kucherov's reaction:
$\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv CH + H_2O \xrightarrow{Hg^{2+}/H^+} [CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2] \xrightarrow{tautomerism} CH_3-CO-CH_3}$ (Propanone).

questions.stem: When propyne is treated with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the presence of $\text{HgSO}_4$, the major product formed is:
questions.solution:
Hydration of propyne (Kucherov reaction) goes via Markovnikov's addition of water to form an enol intermediate:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-C}\equiv\text{CH} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{H}^+, \text{Hg}^{2+}} [\text{CH}_3\text{-C(OH)=CH}_2] \xrightarrow{\text{tautomerism}} \text{CH}_3\text{-CO-CH}_3$ (Propanone).

questions.stem: The major product formed in the reaction of propyne with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ in the presence of $\mathrm{HgSO_4}$ is:
questions.solution: Hydration of propyne (Kucherov's reaction) involves Markovnikov addition of water to give an enol intermediate: $\mathrm{CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2}$, which tautomerizes to the more stable ketone, acetone ($\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_3}$).

questions.stem: An organic compound with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_8$ on treating with sodium metal in liquid ammonia gives a sodium salt. The same compound on hydration with $\mathrm{Hg}^{2+}/\mathrm{H}^+$ gives a ketone. The total number of possible isomers (including stereoisomers) of this compound is _________.
questions.solution:
The compound has formula $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_8$ (Degree of Unsaturation = 2).
It reacts with sodium metal in liquid ammonia, showing it is a terminal alkyne.
Hydration of terminal alkynes gives methyl ketones.
Let's write all possible terminal alkynes of formula $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_8$:
1) Pent-1-yne: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-C\equiv CH}$
2) 3-Methylbut-1-yne: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH-C\equiv CH}$
Neither has any chiral center. Thus, the total number of possible structures/isomers fitting the description is 2.

questions.stem: Propyne on hydration in the presence of $1\%\ \text{HgSO}_4$ and dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives:
questions.solution: Hydration of propyne ($\text{CH}_3\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$) follows Markovnikov's rule to give an unstable enol intermediate: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C(OH)}=\text{CH}_2$, which tautomerizes to the more stable keto form, propan-2-one (acetone).

questions.stem: An alkyne $\mathrm{C_5H_8}$ on treatment with hot acidic $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ gives $2$-methylpropanoic acid and $\mathrm{CO_2}$. The number of $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridized carbon atoms in the starting alkyne is _________.
questions.solution:
Oxidative cleavage of a terminal alkyne $R-\mathrm{C\equiv CH}$ with hot acidic $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ yields $R-\mathrm{COOH}$ and $\mathrm{CO_2}$.
Since the products are $2$-methylpropanoic acid and $\mathrm{CO_2}$, the starting alkyne is $3$-methylbut-1-yne, $(CH_3)_2CH-C\equiv CH$.
In this alkyne, the carbon atoms are $sp^3$ hybridized (in the isopropyl group) and $sp$ hybridized (at the triple bond).
Therefore, the number of $sp^2$ hybridized carbon atoms in the starting alkyne is $0$.

questions.stem: When propyne is treated with dilute $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$ in the presence of $\mathrm{HgSO}_4$ at $333\ \mathrm{K}$, the main product formed is:
questions.solution: Hydration of propyne (Kucherov reaction) using $\mathrm{Hg}^{2+}/\mathrm{H}^{+}$ adds a water molecule across the triple bond according to Markovnikov's rule, forming an enol $[\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})=\mathrm{CH}_2]$ which tautomerizes to the more stable ketone, propanone $(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COCH}_3)$.

questions.stem: Which of the following hydrocarbons will give a red precipitate with ammoniacal cuprous chloride solution?
questions.solution: Terminal alkynes contain acidic hydrogens and react with ammoniacal cuprous chloride to form a red precipitate of copper acetylides. Propyne ($\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv CH}$) is a terminal alkyne and will give a positive test.

questions.stem: When propyne is treated with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ in the presence of $\mathrm{HgSO_4}$, the major product formed is:
questions.solution: Hydration of propyne ($\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv CH}$) with $\mathrm{H_2SO_4/Hg^{2+}}$ occurs via Kucherov's reaction. It undergoes Markovnikov addition of water to form an unstable enol: $\mathrm{CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2}$, which tautomerizes to the stable ketone, propanone (acetone, $\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_3}$).

questions.stem: When propyne is treated with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ in the presence of $\mathrm{HgSO_4}$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.solution: Hydration of propyne ($\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv CH}$) using Kucherov's reaction conditions ($\mathrm{Hg^{2+}/H^+}$) gives an unstable enol intermediate $\mathrm{CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2}$, which tautomerizes to propanone (acetone, $\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_3}$).

questions.stem:
In the following reaction sequence, the total number of $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridized carbon atoms in the final major product '$\mathrm{B}$' is _________.
$$\mathrm{Propyne} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{H_2SO_4}]{\mathrm{Hg^{2+}, H^+}} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow[\text{dil. } \mathrm{NaOH}]{\Delta} \mathrm{B}$$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Hydration of propyne ($\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv CH}$) yields propan-2-one (acetone, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$) as 'A'.
Step 2: Dilute $\mathrm{NaOH}/\Delta$ on acetone is Aldol condensation:
$2\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{OH^-}/\Delta} (\mathrm{CH_3)_2C=CH-CO-CH_3}$ (Mesityl oxide) as 'B'.
In mesityl oxide:
- The two methyl carbons on the double bond are $\mathrm{sp^3}$ hybridized (2 carbons).
- The carbonyl methyl carbon is $\mathrm{sp^3}$ hybridized (1 carbon).
- The two double-bonded carbons are $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridized (2 carbons).
- The carbonyl carbon is $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridized (1 carbon).
Total $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridized carbon atoms $= 2 + 1 = 3$.
